blocks.text: REACH.ai scans a salon’s live appointment book for last-minute openings and cancellations, then contacts the customers most likely to fill them, using machine learning. It is a two-sided platform, and I designed both sides as lead product designer.

items: Consumer side, 0-to-1: the AI booking flow, built from scratch
Business side: a redesign of the merchant dashboard, from discovery to wireframes and UI
Foundation: one visual language and atomic design system for both sides

items.label: steps to book a last-minute appointment
step to sign in with SSO

blocks.text: Last-minute cancellations leave revenue-generating slots unfilled, and the usual response is slow and impersonal. Even when a platform promises AI-driven re-engagement, owners need to see what it earned.

groups.heading: Consumer side
items: Customers wanted booking to be easy, with the provider they already know
One flow had to handle every situation, from email or SMS
Keep it simple and cut drop-off

groups.heading: Business side
items: A noisy dashboard at peak hours
Several complex communication tools
Appointment details spread across systems

blocks.quote: “I need an easy-to-use interface to gain quick, high-level insights into our client’s booking habits and how it affects our stylist’s schedule.”

groups.heading: Frustrations
items: Several complex communication tools
A noisy dashboard at peak hours
Appointment details spread across systems

groups.heading: Goals
items: Surface information to the owner on request
Fewer inbound calls and emails about bookings
Fewer front-desk interruptions

blocks.text: We couldn’t afford formal user testing. For the business side, customer success ran a mixed-methods study with 52 customers, asking the same three questions during sales and support calls, and I reviewed the existing designs against usability heuristics. For the consumer side, I studied competitor booking flows and mapped sitemaps and navigation.

items: “There is a lot of information on the dashboard.”
“I can’t find what I’m looking for.”
“It’s difficult to change locations.”

image.alt: Annotated REACH.ai dashboard with heuristic findings

items: Simplify the color palette

Optimize for mobile
Remove unnecessary and legacy features
Reduce the amount of content on the page
Establish consistent status color, type, and confirmation patterns

blocks.text: I planned and led a 3-day onsite workshop in Phoenix, Arizona to review the experience and find where to improve it. Activities included stakeholder alignment, research synthesis, dot voting, sketching, crazy-eights, critique, and a retro.

image.alt: Workshop participants reviewing sticky notes on a wall
Overlapping dashboard wireframes showing revenue overview and location selector

blocks.text: I set up the visual system from scratch, then built both products on top of it at the same time. High-fidelity UI brought breathing room, confident typography, and one set of components for charts, status, and AI moments.

blocks.text: A brand new booking experience, built from the ground up and tested as it grew.
Customers search by service or provider, so finding the right opening is quick.

blocks.text: A simple 3-step flow (find, review, confirm) keeps last-minute booking pleasant.

blocks.text: Users wanted to see a provider at a specific time, so we added a waitlist. After testing, it didn’t significantly impact bookings and was removed.

image.alt: Waitlist join, phone number, and confirmation screens

blocks.text: Simplifying sign-in to a single SSO step significantly reduced drop-off.
